label: cor:valuative-series-new
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:valuative-series-new}
The coarse Hilbert series of the rank-one-link strand and the full polynomial
$\mathscr C_M$ are valuative after fixing $r$ and $n$. The profile is not
determined by the Tutte polynomial: the two graphic matroids in
Theorem~\ref{thm:Tutte-contrast} have the same Tutte polynomial but different
values of $\Theta$, hence different profiles.
head: environment
name: Valuative rank-one obstruction series

title: Proof
body_md:
The first assertion follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:valuative-profile-new}
and the rank-one-link Hilbert-series formula.  The second follows because
$\Theta$ is a specialization of the profile and is not determined by the
Tutte polynomial.
head: environment

label: prop:valuativity-boundary
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:valuativity-boundary}
Let $p_d(M)$ denote the number of independent $(r-1)$-sets $A$ with
$d_A=|E\setminus\operatorname{cl}_M A|=d$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)}]
\item $p_d(M)=a_{c+1-d}(M)$ for all $d$.  Hence the obstruction profile is
valuative for fixed rank and ground-set size, although it is not
log-concave.
\item The global pair rank $\mathfrak q$ is not valuative.  In the split
subdivision of the base polytope of $U_{2,6}$ along $x_1+x_2+x_3=1$, the
maximal cells are the polytopes of the two rank-two matroids with class
profile $(3,1,1,1)$, and their common face is the polytope of
$U_{1,3}\oplus U_{1,3}$.  The valuative relation
$f(U_{2,6})=f(M_1)+f(M_2)-f(M_{12})$ holds for $\Theta$, with
$120=60+60-0$, but fails for $\mathfrak q$, with $120\ne51+51-0$.
\item $\mathfrak q$ is not determined by the Tutte polynomial: the two
Tutte-equivalent graphic matroids of Theorem~\ref{thm:Tutte-contrast} have
$\mathfrak q=2009$ and $\mathfrak q=2165$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: The boundary of valuativity

title: Proof
body_md:
For (1), mapping $A$ to its closure is a bijection from the independent
$(r-1)$-sets with $d_A=d$ to the pairs consisting of a hyperplane $H$ with
$|E\setminus H|=d$ and a basis of $M|H$.  Hence $p_d=a_{c+1-d}$, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:valuative-profile-new} gives valuativity. For the rank-two
matroid with class sizes $(3,1,1)$, the complete profile is
\[
(p_0,\ldots,p_5)=(0,0,3,0,2,0),
\]
which is not log-concave. Indeed, the three points in the large class have
complementary cocircuit size two, and the other two points have
complementary cocircuit size four.

For (2), a basis of the first cell matroid is a pair containing at most one
element of $\{1,2,3\}$, a basis of the second is a pair containing at most
one element of $\{4,5,6\}$, and the common face consists of the pairs
containing exactly one element of each; this is the standard split
subdivision.  The values of $\mathfrak q$ follow from
Corollary~\ref{cor:rank-two-pure-pair-rank} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:pair-rank-direct-sum}, and the values of $\Theta$ from
Proposition~\ref{prop:rank-two-closed-form} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:Theta-direct-sum}.  A valuative invariant satisfies the
displayed inclusion--exclusion relation, so $\mathfrak q$ is not valuative.

For (3), evaluate \eqref{eq:pair-dim} on the two matroids; the exact
computation is recorded in Section~\ref{sec:verification}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
In characteristic zero, Ilten, Meazzini, and Petracci prove that, for
$i\ge2$, a fine component of $T^i$ vanishes if one negative coordinate
has multiplicity at least $i$ \cite[Theorem~5.1]{IltenMeazziniPetracci}.
Consequently, if $\mathbf c$ has a nonempty negative support, a component
of $T^i$ on the ray $m\mathbf c$, with $m\ge1$, can be nonzero only when
$m<i$. The $i=2$ vanishing used in Section~\ref{sec:cup} holds over every
field by the support criterion for $T^2$.
head: environment
name: Higher diagonal sparsity

label: lem:graph-trichotomy
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:graph-trichotomy}
Let $N$ have rank $s\ge2$, let $B\ne\varnothing$, and let $H$ be a
hyperplane avoiding $B$. Put $b=\operatorname{rk}_N B$. The graph $\Gamma_B(H)$ is
empty if $b\le1$, nonempty and discrete if $b=2$, and nonempty and connected if $b\ge3$.
head: environment
name: Trichotomy for the hyperplane graphs

title: Proof
body_md:
A rank-$(s-2)$ flat gains at most $b$ ranks upon adjoining $B$.
This proves the first assertion. Two distinct such flats have intersection
rank at most $s-3$, so their intersection cannot span with a rank-two set.
For $s=2$ there is at most one rank-zero flat, and discreteness still holds.
When $b=2$, the matroid $(N/B)|H$ has rank $s-2$. A basis of it
is independent in $N$, spans with $B$, and closes inside $H$ to a
qualifying rank-$(s-2)$ flat. Thus the discrete graph is nonempty.

Suppose $b\ge3$ and put $Q=(N/B)|H$. Since $H\cup B$ spans $N$, the
rank of $Q$ is $d=s-b$. Every vertex $G$ contains a basis $I$ of $Q$:
indeed $\operatorname{rk}_QG=\operatorname{rk}_N(G\cup B)-b=d$. Such a basis is also independent
in $N$. Vertices containing the same $I$ form a clique, since
$\operatorname{rk}_N(I\cup B)=s$. The basis-exchange graph of $Q$ is connected.
If $I,J$ are adjacent bases, then $|I\cup J|=d+1\le s-2$.
Extend their closure inside $H$ to a rank-$(s-2)$ flat $K$.
It contains both bases and is a vertex of $\Gamma_B(H)$, joining the
two cliques. Every vertex belongs to one of these cliques. Extending
any basis of $Q$ also proves nonemptiness. If $d=0$, all vertices lie
in the clique corresponding to the empty basis.
head: environment

label: thm:rank-two-support
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:rank-two-support}
Let $N=M^*$. A nonzero component $T^2_{\mathbf a-\mathbf 1_B}(M)$ has
$\operatorname{rk}_N B=2$. Subject to the support conditions of
Theorem~\ref{thm:universal-graph}, put $N_A=(\operatorname{lk}_M A)^*$, where
$A=\operatorname{supp}\mathbf a$. If $\operatorname{rk}_N B=2$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rank-two-flat-count}
T^2_{\mathbf a-\mathbf 1_B}(M)\cong
\bigoplus_{\substack{H\text{ hyperplane of }N_A\\H\cap B=\varnothing}}
k^{\mathcal G_B(H)}/k\mathbf 1,
\qquad
\dim_kT^2_{\mathbf a-\mathbf 1_B}(M)=
\sum_{H\cap B=\varnothing}(|\mathcal G_B(H)|-1)_+.
\end{equation}
Empty blocks contribute zero. Every nonzero $T^1$ component has negative
support of rank one in $N$.
head: environment
name: Rank-two negative support

title: Proof
body_md:
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:graph-trichotomy} to the universal graph formula.
Singleton negative supports have zero $T^2$ by
\eqref{eq:singleton-formula}; dual ranks below two are covered by the
same formula. To compare the dual ranks before and after passing to a
link, let $D$ be the loops of $M/A$. They are coloops of $N\setminus A$,
and $N_A=(N\setminus A)/D$. Deletion leaves the ranks of subsets of
$E\setminus A$ unchanged, and contracting coloops leaves the ranks of
subsets disjoint from $D$ unchanged. Thus $\operatorname{rk}_{N_A}B=\operatorname{rk}_NB$ for
every admissible $B$. The last assertion follows from
\eqref{eq:universal-T1}: if $\operatorname{rk}_NB\ge2$, every eligible graph is
nonempty, whereas rank-zero $B$ lies in every hyperplane. For singleton
supports use \eqref{eq:singleton-formula}. This is a reformulation of
the first-cohomology description of Brehm and Constantinescu
\cite[Theorem~4.7]{BrehmConstantinescu}, not an additional $T^1$ theorem.
head: environment

label: thm:negative-primary-image
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:negative-primary-image}
Let $N=M^*$ and let $\mathbf c=\mathbf a-\mathbf 1_B$ have disjoint
nonnegative parts. If $B$ meets at least three nonloop parallel classes
of $N$, then $\Omega_{\mathbf c}=0$. If $B$ contains a loop of $N$,
then $T^2_{-\mathbf 1_B}=0$. Otherwise,
\[
\Omega_{-\mathbf 1_B}=
\begin{cases}
T^2_{-\mathbf 1_B}(M),&B\text{ meets exactly two parallel classes},\\
0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
In particular, for simple $N$ every purely negative support of size at
least three is invisible to the primary cup product.
head: environment
name: The purely negative primary image

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem~\ref{thm:rank-two-support}, the negative support of a nonzero
$T^1$ class is confined to one nonloop parallel class of $N$.
Every element of $B$ must occur in a negative support of one of the two
factors. Two factors can therefore cover at most two parallel classes,
even when positive and negative supports cancel outside $B$.

Suppose $B=B_1\sqcup B_2$, with nonempty $B_i$ contained in distinct
parallel classes $P_i$, and choose $p_i\in B_i$. A circuit of $M$,
being a cocircuit of $N$, contains either all of $P_i$ or none of it.
Consequently multiplication induces
\begin{equation}\label{eq:parallel-reduction-maps}
x_{B_i\setminus\{p_i\}}:T^1_{-\mathbf 1_{B_i}}\twoheadrightarrow
T^1_{-\mathbf e_{p_i}},\qquad
x_{B\setminus\{p_1,p_2\}}:T^2_{-\mathbf 1_B}\xrightarrow{\sim}
T^2_{-\mathbf e_{p_1}-\mathbf e_{p_2}}.
\end{equation}
For completeness these are maps, not just equalities of dimensions.
In the monomial presentation, a union of circuits contains $B_i$ if
and only if it contains $p_i$. After deleting either $B_i$ or $p_i$,
the resulting monomial is divisible by no circuit meeting $P_i$;
circuits disjoint from $P_i$ are unaffected. The valid Taylor cochain
coordinates and their incidence matrices therefore agree. For the
Koszul conditions the relevant exponents on $P_i$ are uniformly zero,
one, or two before deletion. In each case deleting $B_i$ or just $p_i$
gives the same test for divisibility by a circuit. Thus the same
identification respects the Koszul quotient defining $T^2$.
Multiplication is the identity on these coordinates. For $T^1$, the
singleton target additionally quotients by the derivation image when
$|B_i|>1$, giving the stated surjection.

Lift the two factors of every singleton-pair cup product through
\eqref{eq:parallel-reduction-maps}. Its $R$-bilinearity and the target
isomorphism, together with Theorem~\ref{thm:pure-pair-surjectivity},
prove surjectivity at $-\mathbf 1_B$. If $B$ contains a loop of $N$, no
hyperplane avoids it, so the target is zero. If $B$ meets at most one
parallel class, the target also vanishes by rank-two support.
head: environment

label: lem:negative-generation
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:negative-generation}
Let $\mathbf a\ge0$ and $B\ne\varnothing$, with
$\operatorname{supp}\mathbf a\cap B=\varnothing$. Multiplication induces a surjection
\[
x^{\mathbf a}:T^1_{-\mathbf 1_B}(M)\twoheadrightarrow
T^1_{\mathbf a-\mathbf 1_B}(M).
\]
Consequently $T^1(M)$ is generated as a $k[M]$-module by its purely
negative components.
head: environment
name: Generation of first cohomology

title: Proof
body_md:
The support criterion and Theorem~\ref{thm:rank-two-support} reduce
the assertion to $B$ contained in one nonloop parallel class $P$ of
$N=M^*$. Put $S=k[x_e:e\in E]$ and use the minimal circuit generators
$x_C$ of $I_M$. A circuit contains either all of $P$ or none of it.
Every $C$ containing $B$ has $C\setminus B\in M$: its complement is
$H\cup B$, where $H=E\setminus C$ is a hyperplane avoiding $P$,
and $H\cup B$ spans $N$.

For distinct circuits $C,D$, write $K=E\setminus D$ and $s=\operatorname{rk} N$.
If $B\subseteq C\cup D$, then
\[
\operatorname{rk}_N((H\cap K)\cup B)\le s-2+1<s.
\]
Thus $(C\cup D)\setminus B$ is a nonface of $M$. The evaluated
Taylor pair relation in degree $-\mathbf 1_B$ is therefore zero in $R$;
the same holds after adding $\mathbf a$. If $B\not\subseteq C\cup D$,
that relation has no output monomial of nonnegative degree. When
$s=1$, there is at most one circuit and no distinct pair to check.
Taylor pair relations generate the first syzygies. It follows that
$\operatorname{Hom}_S(I_M,R)_{-\mathbf 1_B}$ is the full coordinate space
on the circuits containing $B$, whereas its degree
$\mathbf a-\mathbf 1_B$ part retains precisely those coordinates with
$(C\setminus B)\cup\operatorname{supp}\mathbf a\in M$. Multiplication by
$x^{\mathbf a}$ is the coordinate projection and is surjective.
The map $\operatorname{Der}_k(S,R)\to\operatorname{Hom}_S(I_M,R)$
is $R$-linear, so this surjection descends to its cokernel $T^1$.
All other fine degrees of $T^1$ vanish by the support criterion.
head: environment

label: thm:full-primary-image
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:full-primary-image}
Let $N=M^*$, and let $p_N(B)$ be the number of nonloop parallel
classes of $N$ met by $B$. For every fine degree
$\mathbf c=\mathbf a-\mathbf 1_B$ with disjoint nonnegative parts,
\[
\Omega_{\mathbf c}=\begin{cases}
T^2_{\mathbf c}(M),&p_N(B)=2,\\
0,&p_N(B)\ne2.
\end{cases}
\]
Degrees excluded by the support criterion have zero target, including
degrees with nonsquarefree negative part. The target also vanishes
if $B$ contains a loop of $N$.
head: environment
name: The primary image in every fine degree

title: Proof
body_md:
The argument in Theorem~\ref{thm:negative-primary-image} excludes
every factorization when $p_N(B)\ge3$. Each element of $B$ must
belong to the negative support of a factor, and two nonzero $T^1$
factors cover at most two dual parallel classes. This remains true
with cancellation outside $B$. Homogeneous tensors span the image;
an $R$-multiple can be absorbed into one factor.

Suppose $p_N(B)=2$ and the target is admissible and potentially
nonzero. Write $B=B_1\sqcup B_2$ according to the two parallel
classes, put $A=\operatorname{supp}\mathbf a$, and let $L=\operatorname{lk}_M A$ on its actual
vertices. If $D$ consists of the loops of $M/A$, then
$L^*=(N\setminus A)/D$. The elements of $D$ are coloops of
$N\setminus A$; deleting $A$ and contracting $D$ preserve the
ranks and parallel-class distinction on $B$.

Set $U=T^1_{-\mathbf 1_{B_1}}(M)$,
$V=T^1_{\mathbf a-\mathbf 1_{B_2}}(M)$, and
$W=T^2_{\mathbf a-\mathbf 1_B}(M)$. Positive-support localization and
Lemma~\ref{lem:negative-generation} give a commuting square
\[
\begin{array}{ccc}
U\otimes_k V&\xrightarrow{\ \cup\ }&W\\
\big\downarrow{\scriptstyle\lambda_1\otimes\lambda_2}&&
\big\downarrow{\scriptstyle\lambda}\\
T^1_{-\mathbf 1_{B_1}}(L)\otimes_k T^1_{-\mathbf 1_{B_2}}(L)
&\xrightarrow{\ \cup\ }&T^2_{-\mathbf 1_B}(L).
\end{array}
\]
Here $\lambda_1$ is multiplication by $x^{\mathbf a}$ followed by
the normalized link isomorphism, hence is surjective;
$\lambda_2$ and $\lambda$ are the normalized link isomorphisms.
To check the degrees and commutativity, localize at $x_A$. In
$R_{x_A}=k[L][x_i^{\pm1}:i\in A]$, the two factors have the form
$\alpha$ and $x^{\mathbf a}\beta$. Their cup is
$x^{\mathbf a}(\alpha\cup\beta)$, and target normalization removes
exactly $x^{\mathbf a}$. The lower cup is surjective by
Theorem~\ref{thm:negative-primary-image} applied to $L$.
Lifting finite sums of its products proves surjectivity onto $W$.
For $p_N(B)\le1$, or for $B$ containing a dual loop, the target
vanishes by Theorem~\ref{thm:rank-two-support} and the graph formula.

label: cor:primary-quotient
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:primary-quotient}
The $R$-module $\Omega$ is generated by its purely negative
components meeting exactly two dual parallel classes. In each
admissible degree $\mathbf c=\mathbf a-\mathbf 1_B$ with $\operatorname{rk}_NB=2$
and $p_N(B)\ge3$, the quotient $Q=T^2(M)/\Omega$ has
\[
Q_{\mathbf c}\cong T^2_{\mathbf c}(M)\cong
\bigoplus_{\substack{H\text{ hyperplane of }(\operatorname{lk}_M A)^*\\
H\cap B=\varnothing}}k^{\mathcal G_B(H)}/k\mathbf 1.
\]
All other components vanish. These are degreewise vector-space
identifications, and the displayed components may themselves be
zero. Their dimensions are independent of the characteristic.

give a nonsquarefree negative part and hence zero target. Theorems
\ref{thm:negative-primary-image}, \ref{thm:full-primary-image}, and

label: thm:cyclic-higher-obstruction
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:cyclic-higher-obstruction}
For every field $k$, the ideal
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cyclic-family}
J=(X,Y,F_jW_{h_0}:j\in L,
              (X/x_j)W_h:j\in L,\ h\ne h_0)
\end{equation}
defines a flat fine-multigraded deformation over $k[t_0,\ldots,t_{m-1}]/(P)$.
Its first-order classes $\alpha_i\in T^1_{-\mathbf e_i}(M_{m,n})$ are nonzero.
Every proper subcollection integrates over its unrestricted polynomial
parameter ring, and all pairwise primary cup products vanish.

Put $\mathfrak m=(t_0,\ldots,t_{m-1})$. The induced deformation over
$k[t]/\mathfrak m^m$ has no lift to $k[t]/\mathfrak m^{m+1}$, even
without requiring the lift to preserve the fine grading. In the
fine-multigraded category its jet modulo $\mathfrak m^m$ is uniquely
determined, up to the usual equivalence, by the first-order classes.
Its first essential obstruction has order $m$ and lies in
$T^2_{-\mathbf 1_L}(M_{m,n})$, a space of dimension $n-1$.
head: environment
name: Cyclic higher obstruction

label: eq:cyclic-identity
title: Proof
body_md:
Shifting the summation index in \eqref{eq:cyclic-polynomials} gives
the telescoping identity
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cyclic-identity}
x_jF_j+t_{j-1}F_{j-1}=X+\sigma P.
\end{equation}
Work first over $B=\mathbb Z[t]/(P)$ and regard the parameters as coefficients.
Choose an order on monomials in $x,y$ refining total degree. The displayed
generators of $J$ are monic and have the leading monomials in
\eqref{eq:two-line-ideal}. We verify the monic Buchberger criterion
over $B$, which is valid over a coefficient ring with zero divisors
because no leading coefficient is divided by a nonunit.

Two unchanged generators have zero S-polynomial. For two modified
generators the S-polynomial is
$W_{h_0}(x_jF_j-x_kF_k)$. Subtracting their identities
\eqref{eq:cyclic-identity} expresses it as a combination of modified
generators with strictly smaller $x,y$ degree than their least common
multiple. For $X$ and a modified generator the same identity gives
a multiple of another modified generator and the remainder
$-\sigma P W_{h_0}=0$. For $Y$ and a modified generator every tail
is divisible by $Y$. Finally, for a modified generator and an unchanged
cross generator with $h\ne h_0$, the least common multiple of $W_h$
and $W_{h_0}$ is $Y$, so every tail is again divisible by $Y$.
These exhaust the S-pairs. Division by a monic basis shows that the
original standard monomials form a $B$-basis of $B[x,y]/J$.
This proves flatness over every field. Setting any parameter to zero
makes $P$ identically zero, proving the proper-subcollection assertion.

The coefficient of $t_i$ in $F_{i+1}$ is
$-X/(x_ix_{i+1})$. Thus $\alpha_i$ is, up to sign, the singleton
hyperplane delta function at $\{i+1,h_0\}$; it is not constant and
is nonzero. Every pair belongs to a proper subcollection, so its
mixed primary obstruction is zero. Each one-parameter restriction is
also a polynomial deformation, so self-obstructions vanish directly,
including in characteristic two.

We next rule out arbitrary, possibly nonhomogeneous, lifts of the
specified jet. Set $A=k[t]/\mathfrak m^{m+1}$. In any flat lift,
choose lifts of the variables and of the displayed ideal generators.
The lifted variables generate the algebra since the base ideal is
nilpotent. Flatness identifies the reduction of its presentation kernel
with $I_{M_{m,n}}$; lifted circuit generators generate that kernel by
the nilpotent form of Nakayama's lemma.
They differ from \eqref{eq:cyclic-family} by parameter monomials of
total degree $m$ with arbitrary coefficients in $k[x,y]$.
Write $g_X$ and $g_{j,h}$ for their coefficients at $P$.
The kernel $\mathfrak m^m$ of $A\to k[t]/\mathfrak m^m$ is
annihilated by $\mathfrak m$. Flatness therefore makes
\[
\mathfrak m^m\otimes_k k[M_{m,n}]\longrightarrow\mathcal A
\]
injective, where $\mathcal A$ is the lifted algebra.
Multiply the modified relation by $x_j$, add $t_{j-1}$ times the
preceding modified relation, and subtract $W_{h_0}$ times the lifted
relation for $X$. By \eqref{eq:cyclic-identity}, its $P$ coefficient
must vanish in the special fiber:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:critical-socle-relations}
\sigma W_{h_0}+x_jg_{j,h_0}-W_{h_0}g_X=0.
\end{equation}
Likewise the unchanged cross relation for $h\ne h_0$ gives
$x_jg_{j,h}-W_hg_X=0$. Corrections at other parameter monomials
do not affect these $P$ coefficients, since a parameter times any
order-$m$ correction is zero in $A$.

Project the first equation to fine degree $\deg W_{h_0}$, and the
second to fine degree $\deg W_h$. No $x_jg_{j,h}$ can contribute,
since the $j$ coordinate of these degrees is zero. If $\lambda$ is
the constant term of $g_X$, the two projections require
$(\sigma-\lambda)W_{h_0}=0$ and $\lambda W_h=0$ in $k[M_{m,n}]$.
Every $W_h$ is a nonzero standard monomial, so $\lambda=\sigma$
and $\lambda=0$, a contradiction over every field. Lifting the
variables presents any abstract affine lift in this form;
thus the contradiction is not restricted to a polynomial ansatz or
to homogeneous correction terms.

It remains to justify uniqueness from the first-order classes in the
stated graded category. For a parameter monomial $t^{\mathbf u}$ of
total degree at least two, $T^1_{-\mathbf u}(M_{m,n})=0$. If $\mathbf u$
is not squarefree this follows from the support criterion; otherwise
its support has rank at least two in the simple dual $N_{m,n}$, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:rank-two-support} applies. Derivations of
$k[x,y]$ into $k[M_{m,n}]$ in degree $-\mathbf u$ are also zero.
Put $S=k[x,y]$ and $R=k[M_{m,n}]$. The presentation exact sequence
\[
\operatorname{Der}_k(S,R)\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Hom}_S(I_{M_{m,n}},R)\longrightarrow T^1(R)
\longrightarrow0
\]
therefore gives $\operatorname{Hom}_S(I_{M_{m,n}},R)_{-\mathbf u}=0$.
Indeed the image of a variable under a derivation would have degree
$\mathbf e_v-\mathbf u$, with a negative coordinate when $|\mathbf u|\ge2$.
Representatives of the same first-order classes can first be aligned
by graded coordinate changes realizing their derivation differences.
Differences between two flat embedded lifts across an order-filtration
small extension lie in these spaces. Induction shows that all
coefficients of orders $2,\ldots,m-1$ are forced. There is no ambiguity
in an ideal-valued coefficient: subtracting a nonempty support from
the degree of a minimal circuit generator leaves either a negative
coordinate or a proper face of that circuit. After choosing the
same first-order representatives, this proves graded uniqueness.
The obstruction has parameter weight $\mathbf 1_L$; its dimension is
computed in Proposition~\ref{prop:two-line-primary-quotient} below.

body_md:

F_0=x_1x_2-t_2x_1+t_2t_1,\quad
F_1=x_0x_2-t_0x_2+t_0t_2,\quad
F_2=x_0x_1-t_1x_0+t_1t_0.

Any two of the three classes integrate jointly, but the specified
second-order deformation has a nonzero cubic lifting obstruction.
The critical block $T^2_{-\mathbf 1_L}$ has dimension two.

name: A six-element cubic obstruction

label: prop:two-line-primary-quotient
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: The quotient missed by the primary cup

title: Proof
body_md:
For $B\subseteq L$ with $|B|\ge2$, the opposite hyperplane $H$
contributes its $n$ rank-one flats as discrete vertices. Each other
hyperplane avoiding $B$ is a cross pair and contributes exactly one
qualifying vertex. This gives dimension $n-1$; interchange the lines
for the second assertion. Every support of size at least three not
confined to one line spans $N_{m,n}$ and has zero $T^2$ by
Theorem~\ref{thm:rank-two-support}. Pair degrees are in $\Omega$,
whereas supports of size at least three are not, by
Theorem~\ref{thm:negative-primary-image}. Counting the remaining
subsets of each line proves \eqref{eq:two-line-primary-quotient}.

label: thm:negative-realization
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:negative-realization}
Let $R=k[M_{m,n}]$ over any field. For $B\subseteq L$ with $|B|=r\ge3$
there is an explicit linear isomorphism
\[
\theta_B:k^H/k\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{\sim}T^2_{-\mathbf 1_B}(R).
\]
Every nonzero $\xi$ in this component is the obstruction of a flat
fine-multigraded deformation over $k[t_i:i\in B]/(t)^r$ to lifting
over $k[t_i:i\in B]/(t)^{r+1}$. More precisely, its obstruction is
$\xi\otimes P_B$, with every other total-degree-$r$ parameter
coefficient zero. This specified jet has no lift even in the ungraded
category. Its $r$ first-order classes are nonzero; every proper
subcollection integrates over its polynomial parameter ring.
The symmetric statement holds for $B\subseteq H$.

Consequently every nonzero homogeneous class of the purely negative
quotient $T^2(R)/\Omega$ is realized in this way, although all primary
cup products among the selected tangent classes vanish.
head: environment
name: Realization in every negative component

label: eq:weighted-cyclic-identity
title: Proof
body_md:
The weighted telescoping identity is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:weighted-cyclic-identity}
x_jF_{j,h}+u_{j-1,h}t_{j-1}F_{j-1,h}=Q+\sigma v_hP_B.
\end{equation}
Over $\mathbb Z[u,t]/(P_B)$, the generators in
\eqref{eq:weighted-cyclic-family} are a monic Gr\"obner basis for
any monomial order in $x,y$ refining total degree. Same-$h$ pairs
of modified generators subtract two identities
\eqref{eq:weighted-cyclic-identity}; the residual terms cancel.
A pair of $X$ and a modified generator has residual
$-\sigma v_hP_BZW_h=0$. A modified and an unchanged cross generator
with the same $h$ use the same identity and have residual
$\sigma v_hP_BZW_h=0$. In each case the predecessor terms have
smaller $x,y$ degree. For different $h$, every tail is divisible by
$Y$, as are the tails in pairs involving $Y$. Pairs of unchanged
monomial generators have zero S-polynomial. These exhaust the pairs,
so the original standard monomials give a free coefficient-module basis.
In particular the family is flat over $k[t]/(P_B)$, and setting any
parameter to zero gives a flat polynomial family.

We identify its actual obstruction in a fixed presentation. Put
$S=k[x,y]$, let $K$ be the relations among the minimal generators of
$I=I_{M_{m,n}}$, and let $K_0$ be their Koszul submodule. The
polynomial-quotient presentation gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:realization-T2-presentation}
T^2(R)=\operatorname{coker}\left(
\operatorname{Hom}_S(S^{2+mn},R)\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Hom}_R(K/K_0,R)\right).
\end{equation}
The Taylor pair relations generate $K$, their triple relations give
the compatibility equations, and Koszul relations impose the additional
annihilation conditions. This low-degree cotangent-complex presentation
is valid for polynomial quotients over any field; no characteristic-zero
comparison or division by an integer is used. We use the monomial
coordinates of \cite[Section~2, Lemma~2]{AltmannChristophersen}.

Orient a Taylor relation as
$R_{p,q}=\operatorname{lcm}(p,q)e_p/p-
\operatorname{lcm}(p,q)e_q/q$. Put $a_j=1$ for $j\in B$ and zero
otherwise. In degree $-\mathbf 1_B$, its residual coordinate is the
coefficient of $\operatorname{lcm}(p,q)/Q$. Define
\begin{align}\label{eq:weighted-obstruction-cochain}
\mu_v(X,C_{j,h})&=-\sigma a_jv_h,\notag\\
\mu_v(C_{j,h},C_{k,h})&=\sigma(a_j-a_k)v_h,
\end{align}
and set all other pair coordinates to zero, with antisymmetry.
Pairs with a negative exponent or nonface shifted support have zero
target and are omitted.

These are coordinates of a cochain in the fixed space
$\operatorname{Hom}_R(K/K_0,R)_{-\mathbf 1_B}$. Indeed the only nonzero
pair targets are within the blocks $\{X,C_{j,h}:j\in L\}$ for fixed
$h$; a pair involving $Y$ or two distinct $h$ has shifted support
containing $Y$. In each block \eqref{eq:weighted-obstruction-cochain}
is the difference of vertex values $0$ at $X$ and $\sigma a_jv_h$
at $C_{j,h}$, so it satisfies every Taylor triangle equation.
A Koszul image on a pair $p,q$ has coefficient monomial $pq/Q$.
For $(X,C_{j,h})$ with $j\in B$, its support contains $C_{j,h}$.
For same-$h$ cross pairs with exactly one index in $B$, it likewise
contains the circuit indexed by that element of $B$. Thus the
nonzero coordinates annihilate the Koszul relations. The remaining
coordinates are zero.

To see that this cochain is the actual lifting obstruction, set
$A_{r-1}=k[t]/(t)^r$ and $A_r=k[t]/(t)^{r+1}$, and write
$d_{j,h}=u_{j-1,h}t_{j-1}$ for $j\in B$, zero otherwise. Lift the
original Taylor relations to
\begin{align*}
\widetilde R_{X,C_{j,h}}&=W_he_X-x_je_{j,h}-d_{j,h}e_{j-1,h},\\
\widetilde R_{C_{j,h},C_{k,h}}&=x_je_{j,h}-x_ke_{k,h}
                   +d_{j,h}e_{j-1,h}-d_{k,h}e_{k-1,h}.
\end{align*}
A predecessor term is included only when its index lies in $B$.
Evaluating at the deformed generators gives respectively
$-\sigma a_jv_hP_BZW_h$ and
$\sigma(a_j-a_k)v_hP_BZW_h$.
For different-$h$ pairs and pairs involving $Y$, the evaluated
Taylor relation is a multiple of $Y$ with coefficient specializing
to zero; subtract that coefficient times $e_Y$ to obtain an exact
relation. The $X,Y$ relation is already exact.

These lifted relations generate the relation module over $A_{r-1}$:
flatness of the quotient implies flatness of its ideal and relation
module in the free presentations, base change recovers $K$, and
nilpotent Nakayama applies to the lifted Taylor generators. The
small-extension obstruction recipe evaluates these relations over
$A_r$ and projects their failures to
$R\otimes_k((t)^r/(t)^{r+1})$. By the displayed evaluations its
class is exactly $[\mu_v]\otimes P_B$, with all other parameter
coefficients zero. Changing generator lifts changes this cochain by
the generator coboundaries in \eqref{eq:realization-T2-presentation}.

We can also read the whole target from this presentation. For fixed
$h$, the triangle equations make any cochain a difference of vertex
values. If $j,k\in B$, the support of $C_{j,h}C_{k,h}/Q$ is
$(L\setminus\{j,k\})\cup(H\setminus\{h\})$, a face: its complement
$\{j,k,h\}$ is a basis of $N_{m,n}$. The Koszul condition therefore
equates the vertex values at all $j\in B$. Generator cochains at
$C_{k,h}$ for $k\notin B$, with values scalar multiples of
$(Z/x_k)W_h$, remove the outside-$B$ vertex values independently.
The generator cochain at $X$, with value a scalar multiple of $Z$,
removes one common constant among the remaining $h$-values.
No other generator has a value in this degree. Hence the entire
quotient is $k^H/k\mathbf 1$, parametrized linearly by $[\mu_v]$.
Explicitly, $\mu_c$ is the coboundary with values $-\sigma cZ$ at
$X$, $-\sigma c(Z/x_k)W_h$ at outside-$B$ cross generators, and
zero elsewhere; a coboundary on the remaining pairs forces all
$v_h$ equal. Thus $\theta_B([v])=[\mu_v]$ is an isomorphism.

Given $\xi\ne0$, choose $[v]=\theta_B^{-1}(\xi)$ and a representative
$v$. Set $u_{i_*,h}=v_h$ for one fixed $i_*\in B$ and set the other
weights to one. A nonconstant vector has a nonzero coordinate.
Every tangent class is nonzero: its value on $X$ is zero, whereas
its value at a successor cross generator with nonzero weight is
$-u_{i,h}XW_h/(x_ix_{i+1})\ne0$. The only polynomial derivation
in degree $-\mathbf e_i$ is a scalar multiple of $\partial/\partial x_i$,
whose nonzero value on $X$ is a scalar multiple of $X/x_i$.
Thus the tangent cannot be a derivation coboundary. Polynomial
integration of every one- and two-parameter restriction proves the
vanishing of the diagonal and mixed primary obstructions in every
characteristic.

Since the obstruction class is nonzero, no lift of this specified
jet exists, regardless of grading. The direct socle argument is also
instructive: if $g_X,g_{j,h}$ are arbitrary coefficients of $P_B$ in
order-$r$ corrections, then for $j\in B$ flatness forces
\[
\sigma v_hZW_h+x_jg_{j,h}-W_hg_X=0.
\]
Projection to fine degree $\deg(ZW_h)$ kills the $x_j$ term and
requires the coefficient of $Z$ in $g_X$ to equal $\sigma v_h$
for every $h$, impossible for nonconstant $v$. This projection
does not require the hypothetical corrections to be homogeneous.
Finally Proposition~\ref{prop:two-line-primary-quotient} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:negative-primary-image} show that the supports just
treated, and their symmetric counterparts, are exactly the nonzero
degrees of the purely negative quotient.

label: cor:realizing-jet-uniqueness
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:realizing-jet-uniqueness}
For the parameters and first-order classes chosen in
Theorem~\ref{thm:negative-realization}, the jet over $k[t]/(t)^r$
is unique up to fine-graded isomorphism inducing the identity on the
special fiber. This does not assert uniqueness among ungraded jets
with the same first-order classes.
head: environment
name: Graded uniqueness of the realizing jets

title: Proof
body_md:
For every parameter weight $\mathbf u$ with $|\mathbf u|\ge2$,
$T^1_{-\mathbf u}(R)=0$: nonsquarefree negative parts vanish by the
support criterion, and squarefree supports of size at least two
have rank at least two in the simple dual, so
Theorem~\ref{thm:rank-two-support} applies. The polynomial
derivations of this degree vanish as well. Align first-order
representatives by graded coordinate changes and apply the
order-filtration induction in the proof of
Theorem~\ref{thm:cyclic-higher-obstruction}; the differences at
each subsequent parameter weight lie in the zero space
$\operatorname{Hom}_S(I,R)_{-\mathbf u}$. This proves the stated
equivalence of the marked jets.
head: environment

label: lem:artinian-relation-lifting
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:artinian-relation-lifting}
Let $A$ be a local Artinian $k$-algebra with residue field $k$, and put
$S=A[z_1,\ldots,z_d]$. Suppose $F_1,\ldots,F_q\in S$ reduce to generators
$p_1,\ldots,p_q$ of $I\subseteq k[z]$. If generators of the relation module
among the $p_i$ lift to exact relations among the $F_i$, then
$S/(F_1,\ldots,F_q)$ is free over $A$ on arbitrary lifts of a $k$-basis of
$k[z]/I$.
head: environment
name: Lifting relations over an Artinian base

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $\mathfrak m$ for the maximal ideal, $J=(F_i)$, and
$K_A=\ker(S^q\to J)$. Right exactness gives
$J/\mathfrak mJ=k[z]^q/\operatorname{im}(K_A\to k[z]^q)$.
The lifted relations imply that this image is the kernel of $k[z]^q\to I$.
Thus $J/\mathfrak mJ\to S/\mathfrak mS$ is injective, and the Tor sequence
gives $\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(S/J,k)=0$ since $S$ is $A$-free.
Let $E$ be the free $A$-module on chosen lifts of a residue-field basis of
$S/J$. The map $E\to S/J$ is surjective: its cokernel equals its product
with $\mathfrak m$, and $\mathfrak m$ is nilpotent. Its kernel $K$ lies in
$\mathfrak mE$ because reduction is an isomorphism. The Tor sequence now
identifies $K/\mathfrak mK$ with $\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(S/J,k)$, so
$K=\mathfrak mK=0$. No finite-dimensionality of the residue-field basis is
required.
head: environment

label: thm:homogeneous-realization
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:homogeneous-realization}
Let $R=k[M_{m,n}]$, $m,n\ge3$, over any field, and let
$\Omega=\operatorname{im}(T^1(R)\otimes_R T^1(R)\to T^2(R))$.
For every fine degree $c$ with $(T^2(R)/\Omega)_c\ne0$, write
$c=a-\mathbf 1_B$, $a\ge0$, with disjoint supports. Then $B$ is contained
in one of the two dual lines, $r=|B|\ge3$, and $\Omega_c=0$, so the
quotient map canonically identifies this component with $T^2_c(R)$.
For every nonzero $\xi$ in it, there is a marked fine-graded flat deformation over
$k[t_i:i\in B]/(t)^r$ whose obstruction to lifting over
$k[t_i:i\in B]/(t)^{r+1}$ is $\xi\otimes[P_B]$ in
$T^2(R)\otimes_k J_r$, where $P_B=\prod_{i\in B}t_i$ and
$J_r=(t)^r/(t)^{r+1}$.
All other total-degree-$r$ obstruction coefficients are zero. This specified
jet has no lift even if grading is forgotten. Its $r$ tangent classes are
nonzero, and every proper subcollection integrates formally. All primary
products among these tangent classes vanish. A cyclic ordering of $B$ and
a distinguished $i_*\in B$ may be chosen arbitrarily; the parameter degrees
are $\deg t_i=\mathbf e_i$ for $i\ne i_*$ and
$\deg t_{i_*}=\mathbf e_{i_*}-a$. In particular $\deg P_B=-c$.

The realizing jet is unique up to marked fine-graded isomorphism for the
chosen parameter degrees and tangent classes. Here isomorphisms are over
the fixed parameter algebra and induce the identity on the special fiber.
A proper subcollection is obtained by setting all other parameters to zero.
The assertion is separate for
each homogeneous degree; it does not assert simultaneous realization of
inhomogeneous sums or describe the full ungraded miniversal base.
head: environment
name: Realization of the homogeneous primary quotient

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $c=a-\mathbf 1_B$ with $a\ge0$ and $\operatorname{supp}(a)\cap B=\varnothing$.
Theorems~\ref{thm:rank-two-support} and \ref{thm:full-primary-image}, with
the actual-vertex convention of \eqref{eq:link-formula}, imply that a nonzero quotient
component has $B$ contained in one dual line, with $r=|B|\ge3$.
Suppose $B\subseteq L$, write $A=\operatorname{supp}(a)$, and put $H_0=H\setminus A$.
If $|H_0|\ge2$, the dual of the actual-vertex link is the deletion $N\setminus A$.
It still has rank three, has no coloops, and consists of the lines
$L\setminus A,H_0$. The only contributing hyperplane is $H_0$, with its
singleton flats as vertices. Hence $T^2_c(R)=k^{H_0}/k\mathbf 1$.
If $|H_0|=1$, its unique point is a coloop of $N\setminus A$; removing that
ghost leaves a rank-two line, whose blocks have at most one vertex and
contribute zero. If $H_0=\varnothing$, $A$ is a nonface and the component
is zero. Thus a nonzero target necessarily has $|H_0|\ge2$.

We need the multiplication map, not merely these dimensions. In the Taylor
presentation on the minimal monomial generating set, modulo Koszul
relations, use \eqref{eq:realization-T2-presentation} and orient
$R_{p,q}=\operatorname{lcm}(p,q)e_p/p-\operatorname{lcm}(p,q)e_q/q$.
Set $b_j=1$ for $j\in B$, zero otherwise, and $\sigma=(-1)^{r-1}$.
The negative cochain representing $v\in k^H$ has coordinates
\[
\mu_v(X,C_{j,h})=-\sigma b_jv_h,\qquad
\mu_v(C_{j,h},C_{k,h})=\sigma(b_j-b_k)v_h,
\]
and zero coordinates elsewhere, as in \eqref{eq:weighted-obstruction-cochain}.
Each scalar multiplies
$\operatorname{lcm}(p,q)/\prod_{i\in B}x_i$.
Multiplication by $x^a$ kills exactly the blocks $h\in A$, because their
monomials become divisible by $Y$. For $h\in H_0$ every same-block Taylor
pair target survives. Its complement contains $B\cup\{h\}$, which spans
$N$, while adding $A$ cannot remove those elements. Taylor triangles make
each surviving block a difference of vertex values; the Koszul conditions
equate all vertices indexed by $B$ since
$(L\setminus\{j,k\})\cup(H\setminus\{h\})$ remains a face after adding
$A$ for distinct $j,k\in B$. Outside-$B$ generator cochains remove their
vertices, and the cochain on $X$ removes one common constant. More explicitly
the vertices of each surviving block are $\{X,C_{j,h}:j\in L\}$; all their
pair and triple targets are nonzero. The cochain values at outside-$B$
generators are scalar multiples of $x^a(Z/x_k)W_h$ for $k\notin B$,
and the value at $X$ is a scalar multiple of $x^aZ$.
Their complements retain $B\cup\{h\}$ and $B\cup H_0$, respectively,
so these are nonzero values. There is no value at $Y$ or a $B$-indexed
cross generator because one negative $B$ coordinate remains. These are
precisely the same operations as in the negative presentation, multiplied
by $x^a$. Consequently the actual multiplication map is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:positive-restriction-map}
k^H/k\mathbf 1\longrightarrow k^{H_0}/k\mathbf 1,
\qquad [v]\longmapsto[v|_{H_0}].
\end{equation}
It is surjective. Since $\Omega_c=0$, choose $v$ with
$[x^a\mu_v]=\xi$; its restriction to $H_0$ is nonconstant.

Fix $i_*\in B$, choose a cyclic ordering, and interpret predecessors and
successors below in that ordering, not in the ground-set labels.
In \eqref{eq:weighted-cyclic-polynomials} set
$u_{i_*,h}=v_hx^a$, $u_{i,h}=1$ for $i\ne i_*$.
Put $Q=\prod_{i\in B}x_i$, $Z=\prod_{i\in L\setminus B}x_i$,
$P_B=\prod_{i\in B}t_i$, and explicitly put
\[
F_{j,h}=\sum_{q=0}^{r-1}(-1)^q
 \left(\prod_{b=1}^q u_{j-b,h}t_{j-b}\right)
 \left(\prod_{i\in B\setminus\{j,j-1,\ldots,j-q\}}x_i\right).
\]
Empty products are one. The constant term is $Q/x_j$ and the
$t_i$-linear term at the successor of $i$ is $-u_{i,h}Q/(x_ix_{i+1})$.
The earlier telescoping identity is a polynomial identity in arbitrary
commuting weights, so substitution of $v_hx^a$ is legitimate. It becomes
\begin{equation}\label{eq:positive-cyclic-identity}
x_jF_{j,h}+u_{j-1,h}t_{j-1}F_{j-1,h}
       =Q+\sigma v_hx^aP_B.
\end{equation}
Use generators $X,Y$, $D_{j,h}=ZF_{j,h}W_h$ for $j\in B$, and
$D_{j,h}=C_{j,h}$ for $j\notin B$. Give $t_i$ degree $\mathbf e_i$ for
$i\ne i_*$ and give $t_{i_*}$ degree $\mathbf e_{i_*}-a$.
Each deformed generator has the fine degree of its original monomial.

Write $k[t]=k[t_i:i\in B]$ and $(t)=(t_i:i\in B)$.
For every $\nu\ge1$, work over $A_\nu=k[t]/((t)^\nu,P_B)$.
All original Taylor pair relations lift exactly, as follows. Put
$d_{j,h}=u_{j-1,h}t_{j-1}$ for $j\in B$; omit predecessor terms entirely
when $j\notin B$.
The $X,D_{j,h}$ relation lifts to
$W_he_X-x_je_{j,h}-d_{j,h}e_{j-1,h}$; evaluation is
$-\sigma b_jv_hx^aP_BZW_h=0$.
For two cross generators in the same block, subtract the corresponding
identities: the lift is
$x_je_{j,h}-x_ke_{k,h}+d_{j,h}e_{j-1,h}-d_{k,h}e_{k-1,h}$
and its evaluation is
$\sigma(b_j-b_k)v_hx^aP_BZW_h=0$.
For a pair involving $Y$, $y_hD_{j,h}$ is divisible by $Y$;
replace the coefficient on $e_Y$ by $y_hD_{j,h}/Y$.
For cross generators in distinct blocks, the original Taylor multipliers
contain the missing $y_h$ and $y_l$. Both evaluated terms are therefore
divisible by $Y$, and their difference divided by $Y$ has zero parameter
constant term. Subtract this quotient times $e_Y$.
The $X,Y$ relation and pairs of unchanged monomials are exact already.
These lifts reduce to every original Taylor pair, which generate all first
syzygies. Lemma~\ref{lem:artinian-relation-lifting} proves $A_\nu$-flatness.
Their formulas are compatible for all $\nu$. The inverse system defines a
formal family over $k[[t]]/(P_B)$; setting any parameter to zero gives a formally
integrated proper subcollection. No polynomial flatness is inferred here.

Over the small extension $k[t]/(t)^{r+1}\to k[t]/(t)^r$, the evaluations
just computed give $[x^a\mu_v]\otimes P_B$. All other pair evaluations
are zero after the exact $Y$ corrections. Over the lower-order jet, flatness
of the quotient makes its ideal flat, and then the relation module in the
free presentation is flat. Reduction is exact and recovers the original
Taylor relations; nilpotent Nakayama shows that their lifts generate this
module. The fixed
small-extension presentation therefore gives precisely $\xi\otimes P_B$
and no other order-$r$ coefficient.

Each ordinary parameter direction has the nonzero tangent class calculated
in Theorem~\ref{thm:negative-realization}.
In the special direction it is multiplied by $x^a$, with weights $v_h$.
Choose $h\in H_0$ with $v_h\ne0$. At the successor cross generator its
value is $-v_hx^aXW_h/(x_{i_*}x_{i_*+1})\ne0$, since the complement of
its support contains the basis $\{i_*,i_*+1,h\}$ of $N$.
Its value on $X$ is zero. The only polynomial derivation of that degree
is a scalar multiple of $x^a\partial/\partial x_{i_*}$, whose value on
$X$ is nonzero: the complement of its support contains $\{i_*\}\cup H_0$,
of rank three. Thus the special tangent is not a derivation coboundary.
Formal one- and two-parameter integration kills the quadratic obstructions.
Their polarization is the cup product by Lemma~\ref{lem:graded-polarization},
also in characteristic two; self-cups vanish by the doubled fine degree.

Since the obstruction class is nonzero, the specified jet has no ungraded
lift. Equivalently, let $g_X,g_{j,h}$ be arbitrary $P_B$ coefficients of
prospective order-$r$ generator corrections. Order-$r$ changes of relation
coefficients evaluate to zero in $R$, and positive-order coefficients times
order-$r$ generator corrections have order at least $r+1$.
Thus arbitrary relation corrections cannot evade the following equation.
Projection of the lifted
$X,D_{j,h}$ relation to $R\otimes P_B$ forces
$\sigma v_hx^aZW_h+x_jg_{j,h}-W_hg_X=0$ for $j\in B$, $h\in H_0$.
The coefficient of $x^aZW_h$ in the $x_j$ term is zero because
$a_j=0$ and $j\notin\operatorname{supp}(ZW_h)$.
Hence the coefficient of $x^aZ$ in $g_X$ must equal $\sigma v_h$ for all
$h\in H_0$, contrary to nonconstancy.

Finally a correction at parameter monomial $t^{\mathbf u}$, $|\mathbf u|\ge2$,
has ring degree $-\sum_i u_i\mathbf e_i+u_{i_*}a$. Its negative part is either
nonsquarefree or meets at least two distinct parallel classes of the
simple dual: its entries on $B$ are exactly $-u_i$, since $a$ vanishes
there. The support criterion in Section~\ref{sec:preliminaries} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:rank-two-support} give $T^1=0$ in these degrees.
A polynomial derivation has no coefficient monomial in such a degree,
because adding one $\mathbf e_j$ cannot make all entries nonnegative.
The right-exact sequence
\[
\operatorname{Der}_k(k[x,y],R)\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Hom}_{k[x,y]}(I,R)\longrightarrow T^1(R)\longrightarrow0
\]
therefore gives a zero correction space.
Aligning first-order representatives by marked graded coordinate changes
and inducting through parameter orders $2,\ldots,r-1$ gives marked fine-graded uniqueness,
without asserting ungraded uniqueness. The case $B\subseteq H$ follows
by interchanging the two lines.

label: thm:primary-quotient-module
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:primary-quotient-module}
For $m,n\ge3$ and every field $k$, there is a fine-graded $R$-module
isomorphism
\begin{equation}\label{eq:primary-quotient-module}
\mathcal Q\simeq
\left((S_L/J_L)\otimes U_H\right)\langle-\mathbf1_L\rangle
\ \oplus\
\left(U_L\otimes(S_H/J_H)\right)\langle-\mathbf1_H\rangle.
\end{equation}
The indicated $S$-modules are annihilated by $I$, so their $R$-module
structures are unambiguous. The quotient has exactly $m+n-2$ minimal
homogeneous generators: $n-1$ in degree $-\mathbf1_L$ and $m-1$ in degree
$-\mathbf1_H$. Its annihilator in $S$ is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:primary-quotient-annihilator}
\operatorname{Ann}_S \mathcal Q=(J_LS+K_HS)\cap(K_LS+J_HS).
\end{equation}
Consequently $\operatorname{Ann}_R \mathcal Q$ is this ideal modulo $I$.
The annihilator is radical. Every irreducible component of
$\operatorname{Supp}_R \mathcal Q$ has dimension $m+n-5$; in particular the support
of the primary quotient has codimension two in $\operatorname{Spec}R$.

name: Generators, relations, and support of the primary quotient

title: Proof
body_md:
Use the Taylor presentation \eqref{eq:realization-T2-presentation},
with $R_{p,q}=\operatorname{lcm}(p,q)e_p/p-
\operatorname{lcm}(p,q)e_q/q$. Its coboundary is
$\delta f(R_{p,q})=(\operatorname{lcm}(p,q)/p)f(p)
 -(\operatorname{lcm}(p,q)/q)f(q)$.
Normalize the cocycle \eqref{eq:weighted-obstruction-cochain} by removing
its factor $(-1)^{|B|-1}$. The resulting $\nu_B(v)$ has scalars
\[
\nu_B(v)(X,C_{j,h})=-b_jv_h,\qquad
\nu_B(v)(C_{j,h},C_{k,h})=(b_j-b_k)v_h,
\quad b_j=\mathbf1_{j\in B},
\]
and zero elsewhere; each scalar multiplies $\operatorname{lcm}(p,q)/x_B$.

We first determine multiplication when a negative coordinate is removed;
this is the point not supplied by the component dimensions. Suppose
$B\subseteq L$, $|B|\ge3$, $i\in B$, and $B'=B\setminus\{i\}$.
In the fixed Taylor presentation let $f_i(v)$ be the generator cochain
of degree $-\mathbf1_{B'}$ given by
\[
f_i(v)(C_{i,h})=v_h C_{i,h}/x_{B'}\quad(h\in H),
\qquad f_i(v)(X)=f_i(v)(Y)=f_i(v)(C_{j,h})=0\quad(j\ne i).
\]
Its nonzero monomials are defined, since $i\notin B'$; their complements
are $B'\cup\{i,h\}$ and span $N$, so they survive in $R$.
For $|B'|\ge3$ the cocycle formulas give the identity
\begin{equation}\label{eq:negative-coordinate-boundary}
x_i\nu_B(v)-\nu_{B'}(v)=\delta f_i(v).
\end{equation}
Indeed, measured relative to $\operatorname{lcm}(X,C_{i,h})/x_{B'}$,
the change at $(X,C_{i,h})$ is $-v_h$, precisely the scalar
of the boundary $-x_if_i(v)(C_{i,h})$. On a same-$h$ pair it is the
difference of the two changed vertex scalars. Every other pair involving
one of the selected generators has its target divisible by $Y$ and hence
zero in $R$: this includes pairs with $Y$ and cross pairs in distinct
$h$ blocks. All remaining values on both sides are zero. Thus the actual
map on the coordinate quotient is $[v]\mapsto[v]$.
When $|B'|=2$, the target has zero primary quotient, so the map into $\mathcal Q$
is zero without any comparison of cocycle normalizations in that degree.
Multiplying these identities by a positive monomial preserves them,
including when some generator values vanish. Multiplication in a
same-line positive coordinate leaves the remaining coordinate quotient
unchanged. An opposite-line coordinate $y_h$ restricts the quotient on
$H_0$ to that on $H_0\setminus\{h\}$. If $h$ is already absent it leaves
the coordinates unchanged; if at most one remains, the target is zero.
Subsequent powers therefore act identically on the surviving coordinates. These
last assertions follow from the actual restriction map
\eqref{eq:positive-restriction-map}.

Send $e_h$ in the first summand of \eqref{eq:primary-quotient-module}
to $[\nu_L(\mathbf e_h)]\in\mathcal Q_{-\mathbf1_L}$.
The common-constant relation is zero, and $y_he_h$ maps to zero by
coordinate restriction. A generator $x_D$ of $J_L$ removes $m-2$
negative coordinates, leaving two; hence it maps every $e_h$ to zero.
This defines an $S$-linear map from the presented module, before any
dimension comparison. The symmetric construction defines the second map.

For $b\ge0$, the degree-$b$ component of $U_H$ is the coordinate space
on $H\setminus\operatorname{supp}(b)$ modulo one common constant, with
dimension $(|H\setminus\operatorname{supp}(b)|-1)_+$.
A degree $c=a-\mathbf1_B$ in the first shifted summand survives the
$J_L$ relation exactly when $B\subseteq L$ and $|B|\ge3$.
Indeed, for unshifted $L$-degree $u\ge0$, $B=\{i:u_i=0\}$ and
$x^u\notin J_L$ is equivalent to $|\operatorname{supp}(u)|\le m-3$.
The $U_H$ factor additionally requires $|H_0|\ge2$.
The actual maps just proved show that its image is all of $\mathcal Q_c$.
The component calculation in Theorem~\ref{thm:homogeneous-realization}
gives equality of dimensions and therefore
injectivity. The nonzero fine degrees of the two summands are disjoint,
so their sum is the required $S$-module isomorphism.

The ideal $I$ annihilates both presented summands directly. In the first,
$X$ and every $C_{j,h}$ have $L$ support of size at least $m-2$ and belong
to $J_LS$, while $Y$ kills $U_H$. In the second, $Y$ and every cross
generator belong to $J_HS$, while $X$ kills $U_L$.
Thus the isomorphism descends to $R$.
Modulo the homogeneous maximal ideal, $U_H$ has exactly its $n$ degree-zero
generators and the single relation $\sum e_h=0$. The first summand has
$n-1$ generators in its lowest degree $-\mathbf1_L$; the second contributes
$m-1$ in degree $-\mathbf1_H$. Graded Nakayama proves the stated minimality.

The annihilator of $U_H$ is fine homogeneous, hence monomial. A monomial
with support $D$ maps the degree-zero coordinate quotient onto the
quotient on $H\setminus D$. Its action is zero exactly when $|D|\ge n-1$;
the degree-zero generators generate the module. Therefore
$\operatorname{Ann}_{S_H}U_H=K_H$.
The same support test shows that the annihilator of the first tensor
summand is $J_LS+K_HS$: a monomial outside this ideal acts nontrivially
on a suitable degree-zero generator. The symmetric formula for the other
summand yields \eqref{eq:primary-quotient-annihilator}.
Both ideals in the intersection are generated by squarefree monomials
and are radical, as is their intersection. The maximal coordinate faces
of $V(J_LS+K_HS)$ have $m-3$ vertices in $L$ and $n-2$ in $H$; those of
$V(K_LS+J_HS)$ have $m-2$ in $L$ and $n-3$ in $H$. No maximal face of either
contains one from the other, and each has $m+n-5$ vertices. The support
is thus pure of that dimension. Finally $R$ is equidimensional of
dimension $\operatorname{rk} M=m+n-3$, proving the codimension assertion.
